# Environment variables — `cloud-security-engineer`

<!-- generated by platform/scripts/gen_env_doc.py from distribution.yaml; do not edit by hand -->

`cloud-security-engineer` reads the following variables from its profile `.env` (generated as `.env.EXAMPLE` on install). All are credentials or endpoints — they are **never committed and never logged**. Set them in `.env`, then forward the names into the Kali sandbox via `docker_forward_env` in `config.yaml`.

## Reference

| Variable | Required | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AWS_PROFILE` | no | — | Named AWS CLI profile for READ-ONLY API queries (read-only IAM principal) |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | no | — | Access key ID of a READ-ONLY AWS principal (SecurityAudit/ViewOnlyAccess); never a write/admin key |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | no | — | Secret key for the READ-ONLY AWS principal above; never printed, logged, or committed |
| `AWS_REGION` | no | `us-east-1` | Default region for the READ-ONLY AWS session; scanners still enumerate all regions |
| `AZURE_TENANT_ID` | no | — | Azure AD tenant ID for the READ-ONLY (Reader-role) service principal |
| `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` | no | — | App/client ID of the READ-ONLY Azure service principal (Reader role only) |
| `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` | no | — | Client secret for the READ-ONLY Azure (Reader) service principal; never printed or committed |
| `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` | no | — | Path to a GCP service-account key file with READ-ONLY (Viewer) role; mounted, never committed |

## `.env` template

Copy into the profile's `.env` and fill real values (do not commit it):

```dotenv
# Other
AWS_PROFILE=   # optional
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=   # optional
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=   # optional
AWS_REGION=us-east-1   # optional
AZURE_TENANT_ID=   # optional
AZURE_CLIENT_ID=   # optional
AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET=   # optional
GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=   # optional
```

## Forward into the sandbox

Add the names (not values) to `config.yaml` so the Kali container sees them:

```yaml
terminal:
  docker_forward_env:
    - AWS_PROFILE
    - AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    - AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    - AWS_REGION
    - AZURE_TENANT_ID
    - AZURE_CLIENT_ID
    - AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET
    - GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
```

## Handling rules

- Credentials come **only** from these env vars — never hard-coded, printed, or committed (platform Security Policy).
- Prefer **read-only / least-privilege** credentials for every integration; forward names into the sandbox via `docker_forward_env`.
- Optional vars left unset simply disable or degrade the feature that needs them.
- Rotate any credential that may have been exposed; `.env` is in `.gitignore` and must stay untracked.
